full_judgment: 7. Mr Ozair Farooq appearing on behalf of the defendant-appellants has taken us to the agreement, applications for time as well as application under section 151 of the Code Civil Procedure for supplying copy of the plaint in 'Bangle Language counter-affidavit, affidavit-in-reply and annexures thereto. Mr. Ozair Farooq also placed the application under section 34 of the Arbitration Act and the written objection filed by the plaintiff-respondent and other materials on record. The learned Advocate for the appellants made two fold submissions in as much as the present defendant-appellants were mere commission agent and signed the contract having been authorised by the principal defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and the period of said letter of authority expired on 31.12.1985 and as such these defendants are neither necessary nor proper party to the suit and considering that aspect of the case these defendants were not make parties before the I.C.C. at Paris. Therefore, the defendants have no liabilities but they are made parties in the suit with malafide motive and the address of the defendant No.1 was given at 5 Bangahondhu Avenue, Dhaka with ulteriar motive. His next submission is that Article 18(1) and Article 18(2) of the contract speak for holding arbitration at Dhaka and without resorting to hold such arbitration at Dhaka the suit cannot be proceeded with. He again submits that the applications seeking time for filing written statements cannot be construed as steps in the proceeding as contemplated under section 34 of the Arbitration Act as the defendants could not understand the contents of the plaint for not being supplied with the plaint in "Bangla' language and that submission of application was not unconditional which will be evident from the averments of the application dated 27.4.1992 and such conduct does not amount "to taking any other steps in the proceedings". The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Subordinate Judge erred in law in rejecting the application under section 34 of the Arbitration Act in not finding in that these defendants were not made parties before the I.C.C. and also the fact that the plaint in "Bangla' language was not supplied before 17.8.1992. In support of his contention Mr. Ozair Farooq referred to certain decisions such as in the cases of Nuruddin Abdulhussain versus Abu Ahmed Abdul Jalli, AIR 1950 (Bom) 127; Food Corporation of India and another versus Yadav Engineer and Contractor, Supreme Court Cases 1982 (2SCC) 499; Badsha Miah Sowdagar versus Nurul Haque and others 18DLR 237; Sea Liberties Inc. versus The Province of East Pakistan and others 19 DLR376; Md. Esack versus Raja Miah and others, 20 DLR 1120; Pioneer Rope Manufacturing Co. Ltd. and others versus Pakistan Industrial Credit and Invest Corporation Ltd. and others, 21 DLR554.
